newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish govt not happy with crown, sees it firming.
newsitem.headline: Swedish govt not happy with crown, sees it firming.

text.p: The Swedish government said on Tuesday that the volatility of the crown was not satisfactory and forecast it would strengthen.

"Even if monetary policy is primarily directed at price stability and so a target for foreign exchange rates does not exist, the instability is not satisfactory," the government said in its supplementary budget proposal.
The crown has softened in recent months in an international financial environment that has been less advantageous than in 1996, the government said.
The crown has weakened 4.78 percent against the mark since October.
At 1250 GMT on Tuesday it was changing hands at 4.4340 to the mark and trading at 120.95 on the trade weighted TCW index.
The government expects the crown to strengthen to 119.2 on the TCW index this year, to 117.9 in 1998 and to 117.0 in both 1999 and 2000.
The central bank, the Riksbank, has no target for the crown, but has set its appropriate nominal TCW index level between 110 and 119, corresponding to an actual range from 109 to 118.
